content:
In https://github.com/leanprover-community/batteries/pull/1954, I added proofs of List.take_flatten (essentially a description of how L.flatten.take i looks like) and several related theorems involving drop, getElem?, and getElem.

In https://github.com/leanprover-community/batteries/pull/1919, it was mentioned that we probably want to relate indexing into a flattened list with Fin.decodeSigma, so I tried to prove that version of getElem_flatten, which I call getElem_flatten_decodeSigma.

I first tried to directly state the necessary lemmas and follow the same induction-based flow, but I immediately hit the roadblock. I tried various alternative definitions to no avail. Often, the subterm that had to be substituted looked correct, yet neither rw nor simp would rewrite it. In other cases I was hit by "motive is not type correct" error with no apparent way forward (I vaguely recall simp didn't solve the problem).

So I switched to an alternative approach: prove that the values of decodeSigma coincide with j and k, respectively. For this, I had to add auxiliary definitions that give the two values as Nat, prove necessary properties on them, and then use them in the usual induction proof.

This means that I do finally have a working proof of getElem_flatten_decodeSigma, but one that depends on getElem_flatten. If I were to prove other related theorems, they would all depend on the *_flattens mentioning those "messy" j and k.

Would such a proof still be a good addition to Batteries?

Hi. Yeah these are good questions. I think if I am honest the current version of getElem_flatten is just not fit for purpose and I don't think your PR will merge until that is sorted. I don't think the proof that you describe is desirable though.

One of the issues is that really we would be better stating this as a lemma on get - the function. It's a lot easier to at least state what you want to be true then.

For what it is worth I think these are the right getElems:

proof_wanted get_flatten (L : List (List α)) :
    L.flatten.get = (fun x => (L.get x.1).get x.2) ∘
    Fin.decodeSigma (length ∘ L.get) ∘ Fin.cast (sum_comp_get L length ▸ length_flatten)

proof_wanted getElem_flatten (L : List (List α)) (i : Nat) (h : i < L.flatten.length) :
    let j : (i : Fin (L.length)) × (Fin (L[i].length)) :=
    Fin.decodeSigma (length ∘ L.get) ⟨i, lt_of_lt_of_eq h (sum_comp_get L length ▸ length_flatten)⟩
    L.flatten[i] = (L.get j.1).get j.2
It would be easier to state this if we had Sigma.curry and Sigma.uncurry in Batteries. I will ask François what he thinks.

I uploaded complete working proofs at https://github.com/Bubbler-4/FlattenTheorems. It contains some lemmas that may be of independent interest, especially those in the OfFn module. There's also a lemma describing the output values of decodeSigma, without mentioning List.flatten.

Side note: In the statement of ofFn_eq_iff', I used "exists" to express a dependent product of Prop and Prop. While it works for the purpose, I feel like it's not the right way to do it...

I agree that the current proof of the main result is not great. But I guess a statement avoiding Fin could have its uses, since working with Fin is simply much harder (might be my skill issue).
Another idea: what if we define the Nat-equivalent of Fin.decodeSigma and use it in the Nat-based statements?
